applies_to: Weil-McLain Evergreen, SlimFit 550-750 Series 2 & 3, SlimFit 1000-2000 Series 2 and SVF boilers, read through a ProtoNode FPC-N34 gateway.
summary: A ProtoNode FPC-N34 reads the boiler control over Modbus RTU and presents it as a BACnet IP or BACnet MS/TP device with 831 objects numbered in one sequence across AI, AV, BI and MI. Besides temperatures, status, counters and lockout history, it carries the priority and network (cascade) settings, a block per cascade member (Shadow 2-8), and bit-level BIs for relay outputs, inputs and lockout causes.
notes: This supplement only lists the objects; device instance, MAC address and baud rate are set on the ProtoNode as described in its start-up guide, which is a separate document.
The same object list is served over BACnet IP or BACnet MS/TP, depending on how the ProtoNode is set up.
No units or state texts are given. The LonWorks types in the source show which values are temperatures, percentages or hours.
The supplement has no read/write column. The 111 AVs map to LonWorks input variables, so they are marked writable; every other object is read-only.
Object IDs run in one sequence (1-831) across AI, AV, BI and MI; each ID is used by one object type only.
Shadow 2-8 blocks repeat the status of the other boilers in a cascade.
SlimFit 1000-2000 Series 1 (SOLA) boilers use a different object list.

integration.summary: Most objects are read-only monitoring. Map boiler status, target and outlet temperatures, modulation rate, gas valve output and sensor warnings. The writable AVs are the priority, network and cascade settings (supply targets, outdoor reset, differentials, rates, times); the supplement does not say which one a BMS should use as a run or setpoint command.

minimum_points.name: Active Target Supply Temperature
minimum_points.why: Supply temperature the boiler is aiming for

setup: Device instance, MAC address and baud rate are set on the ProtoNode (see the ProtoNode start-up guide); this supplement does not list them.
Object IDs are unique across object types (1-831), so AI 7 and AV 7 never both exist.
gotchas: No read/write column: AVs are writable settings, all AI/BI/MI are read-only.
Several names repeat (for example Boiler Status is MI 138 and AI 653, AI 75 Local Return Temp and AI 151 Local Return Temperature); use the object ID, not the name.
Writable AVs are boiler configuration values; avoid writing them cyclically.
